result.title: Perturb, Repair, Verify: Self-Play Vision-Language Verifiers for Compositional Understanding
result.summary: Vision-language verifiers judge whether an image faithfully matches a textual description, yet existing training pipelines typically rely on static supervision from stronger external judges or curated hard-negative data. Such supervision requires external generation or annotation, is teacher-bounded, and is difficult to adapt as model failures evolve. We introduce PROVE (Perturb-and-Repair Optimization for Vision-Language Evaluation), a self-play framework that trains verifiers through a closed perturb-verify-repair-verify loop. Starting from a known-correct image-caption pair, a Mutator introduces a typed perturbation over objects, attributes, counts, or relations. The verifier then judges the perturbed caption and provides textual feedback, which a Repairer uses to recover a faithful caption for re-verification. These two verification rounds produce structured rewards for informative mismatches and visually grounded repairs. Since perturbation, verification, and repair are role-conditioned behaviors of the same evolving multimodal backbone, updating the shared parameters also improves the verifier itself. Experiments show that PROVE improves fine-grained compositional verification across model scales and families and strengthens visual-detail robustness on the reference backbone, with limited, benchmark-dependent changes on broader multimodal tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PROVE 自博弈框架，用「扰动—验证—修复—再验证」闭环训练视觉语言验证器：由同一多模态骨干分别扮演 Mutator、Verifier 与 Repairer，对对象、属性、数量、关系施加类型化扰动，并以两轮验证产生的结构化奖励联合优化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其围绕对象、属性、关系扰动的自博弈验证与结构化奖励，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的视觉证据忠实度校验与训练监督提供线索，但需核查验证反馈是否真正依赖图像细节而非语言先验。
